elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages"
"no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages"

elements.element: Any termination/exit charge on Customer reduced to nil (formula disapplied)
elements.evidence: "the amount of which shall be zero and not an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales ... less $800,000"

elements.element: An early-termination fee exists and is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: Redline eliminates any fee entirely: "the amount of which shall be zero"; no 3-month cap is stated.

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: No liquidated amount is retained; "no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages"

reasons: The single replace operation flips Section 4.2(a) so that the Company (our client, the customer) owes no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages and the Termination Payment amount is zero, satisfying the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

The edit is confined to the operative words of 4.2(a); the term, notice, renewal and payment-schedule mechanics in 4.1 and 4.2(b)-(c) are untouched, and 4.2(b) ('if less than or equal to zero, no Termination Payment shall be due') remains consistent with a zero amount, so no contradiction or dangling obligation arises.

Fallback is not met (and need not be, since the locked target is preferred): no capped early-termination fee is created. The residual negated formula wording ('and not an amount equal to ...') is stylistically clumsy but operatively harmless and is a rationale-level note only.
